audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL transaction processing (London/EIP-1559 fee market, transaction types, gas refunds, access lists), EVM internals (Cancun stack operations), KZG cryptographic primitives for blob transactions, CL validator block proposal with builder bids (Gloas fork), CL data availability sampling (Fulu DAS), CL light client header construction (Capella), wallet chain switching (EIP-2015), block explorer URL routing (EIP-3091), and uncle block RPC responses (EIP-3045).

el_attack_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion via crafted RPC queries, SSRF via wallet chain switching RPC URLs
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks/transactions, provide invalid KZG proofs

cl_attack_vectors.threat: Submit invalid bids, refuse to broadcast DataColumnSidecars after bid acceptance, reference incorrect parent hashes
False payload timeliness attestations, censorship via incorrect data.index signaling
Withhold data columns, serve invalid DataColumnSidecars with bad KZG proofs, data unavailability attacks
Serve fabricated execution payload headers with forged Merkle proofs to light clients

misclassified_entities.reason: Governance process participant, not a runtime external entity interacting with EL/CL protocol at the data plane. EIP submission is a social process, not a protocol boundary.
Client development teams configure activation times as part of the software release process, not at runtime protocol boundaries. This is an operational/governance concern, not a trust boundary.

Internal system component that calls KZG proof verification functions. The actual external entity is whatever submits the blob data (transaction submitter or peer node), not the internal caller of the verification routine.
A blob transaction is a data object, not an external entity. The external entity is the transaction submitter who creates and sends the blob transaction.
This is a threat-modeling label for a DApp, not a distinct entity type. Merged into the general DApp entity with UNTRUSTED trust level, since all DApps must be treated as potentially malicious.

Interacts with block explorer tooling (EIP-3091), which is not part of the EL/CL protocol layer under audit. Block explorers are external applications. However, if the explorer queries the EL via JSON-RPC, that interaction is covered by the RPC client entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user or application can submit transactions via the public JSON-RPC endpoint. No authentication required. Transactions may be legacy, EIP-2930, or EIP-1559 type and must undergo full validation including type detection, signature verification, gas price checks (max_fee >= base_fee), and access list validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Query Client via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External clients querying blockchain data via JSON-RPC. No authentication required. While queries are read-only, malformed inputs (block hashes, uncle indices) must be validated. Response format must correctly handle fork-dependent fields (e.g., baseFee presence based on EIP-1559 activation).

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Wallet RPC (wallet_updateEthereumChain)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps request chain switching via wallet RPC. Fully untrusted: may attempt SSRF via malicious RPC URLs pointing to internal resources, phishing via fake chain parameters mimicking known networks, or URL injection attacks. All provided RPC URLs must be sanitized and validated (HTTPS required, private IP ranges blocked, chainId cross-checked).

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp-Provided RPC Endpoint
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: HTTP/HTTPS connection to external RPC server (via EIP-2015 chain switching)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC endpoints provided by DApps in wallet_updateEthereumChain requests are fully untrusted. The wallet connects to these endpoints to verify chainId. SSRF risk: URL may point to internal services. Response may be spoofed. Must validate URL format, block private IPs, verify net_version and eth_chainId responses match claimed chain.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Payload Builder via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Builders submit signed bids via gossipsub. Fully untrusted: bids may reference incorrect parent hashes, claim amounts exceeding builder balance, or carry invalid signatures. After bid acceptance, the builder is delegated responsibility to broadcast DataColumnSidecars but may fail to do so. Validation required: signature verification, builder balance coverage check, parent hash consistency, and bid validity checks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Gossipsub Network (DAS Column Distribution)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DataColumnSidecars are distributed via gossipsub. Peers on the network are unauthenticated and may send invalid sidecars, withhold data, or flood with garbage. All received columns must be verified against KZG commitments and proofs before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: Column Custody Peers via Req/Resp
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (req/resp protocol for column retrieval)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: When columns are not received via gossip, nodes fall back to direct req/resp queries to peers who custody the needed columns. These peers are untrusted: they may serve invalid data, refuse to respond, or provide columns with invalid KZG proofs. All received data must pass KZG proof verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client via Light Client API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients request headers from full nodes. From the full node's perspective, light client requests are untrusted and may attempt resource exhaustion. From the light client's perspective, the full node serving headers is untrusted and may provide fabricated execution payload headers. Merkle branch proofs must be verified against trusted beacon block body roots.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted Byte Input for KZG Operations
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: KZG precompile / verification functions (blob transactions, point evaluation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Raw byte inputs to KZG cryptographic operations (48-byte G1 points, 32-byte field elements, proof verification inputs) originate from transactions and peer-provided data. All inputs are untrusted: G1 points must be validated on the BLS12-381 curve, field elements must be checked against the BLS modulus, and input lengths must be asserted before cryptographic operations.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal EL attack vector. Peer nodes on the P2P network are unauthenticated and may send invalid blocks, malformed transactions, or attempt eclipse attacks. All received data must be fully validated including transaction type, signature, gas, and state transition rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector. Validators may propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations (slashing condition), or abuse the payload timeliness signaling (setting data.index incorrectly to disrupt fork-choice). Attestation data.index repurposing in Gloas (0=absent, 1=present) creates new attack surface for false payload status signals.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: type detection (legacy/0x01/0x02), RLP decode, signature verification, nonce check, gas limit check, max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee_per_gas (EIP-1559), access list format validation, intrinsic gas calculation including access list costs.

Input validation for block hash format and uncle index. Response must correctly include or omit baseFee field based on EIP-1559 fork activation status. Malformed inputs must not cause crashes or information leakage.

Chain switch requests must be validated: chainId format (0x-prefixed EIP-155), RPC URL sanitization (block private IPs, require HTTPS), cross-check against known chain database for phishing detection. User confirmation required before any chain switch. Error 4001 on rejection.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Outbound HTTP connection from wallet to DApp-provided RPC URL
boundary_edges.security_assumption: SSRF prevention: block localhost, private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x), link-local addresses. Validate URL format. Verify net_version and eth_chainId responses match the claimed chain. Timeout enforcement to prevent resource exhaustion.

Builder bid validation required: cryptographic signature verification, builder balance coverage check (sufficient funds to cover bid amount), parent block hash consistency with current chain head, bid validity period. Proposer must fall back to local block construction if no valid bids received.

All received DataColumnSidecars must be verified against KZG commitments and proofs before acceptance into the local data store. Invalid sidecars must be rejected. Column indices must match the subscribed subnet.

Fallback column retrieval from peers requires same KZG proof verification as gossip-received data. Peers may be unresponsive (timeout handling needed) or serve invalid data. Recovery threshold of >=50% columns must be met before attempting Reed-Solomon reconstruction.

Full node must correctly construct LightClientHeaders with accurate execution payload headers and valid Merkle branch proofs. Light clients must verify execution branch proofs against trusted beacon block body roots. Fork-dependent header format (Capella vs pre-Capella) must be correctly applied.

All byte inputs must be validated before cryptographic operations: 48-byte inputs must be valid BLS12-381 G1 points (check point at infinity special case, then full BLS validation), 32-byte inputs must be less than BLS modulus, input lengths must be exactly 48 or 32 bytes as expected. Trusted setup parameter KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL_1 must not be compromised.

All blocks and transactions received from peers must undergo full validation: block header validation, transaction signature verification, state transition execution, gas accounting (including EIP-1559 effective gas price calculation, 20% refund cap). Eclipse attack mitigation through peer diversity.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P beacon gossip (attestation subnets, payload attestation topic)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Attestations must be validated for correct signature, slot, committee assignment, and beacon block root. Payload timeliness attestations (Gloas) must be from valid PTC members. data.index field (repurposed for payload status signaling: 0=absent, 1=present) must be validated. Conflicting attestations trigger slashing conditions.
